comment: What a resort map pack contains (ADR-036). One source of truth for the pipeline (normalize_osm.py, build-pack.sh), the style generator, write-packs.mjs and the tests. Changing a layer, a field or a zoom here is a schema change: rebuild the packs and the styles. pack_format is the format new builds get (MAPS_PLAN D9); a format, once defined in formats, never changes. roles describes every file role a defined format uses (its file suffix, the pipeline's tile spec, the style's source and placeholder); a pack of format n holds exactly the roles of formats[n].roles. trail_view and style are the trail-map view's contract (docs/MAPS_TRAILVIEW_DESIGN.md), outside formats.

field_notes.piste.rank: importance, from normalize_osm.py: 1 the trunk runs (within each rating as the style colours it, the longest named runs making up half of that rating's named in-bounds run length), 3 runs under 300 m, 2 the others
field_notes.piste.oriented: the line runs downhill as drawn, checked against the elevation model (orient.py); absent when too flat or ambiguous: no arrows
field_notes.lift.oriented: the line runs uphill as drawn, checked against the elevation model (orient.py)
field_notes.lift_station: OpenStreetMap stations within 100 m of a kept lift, and the two ends of every kept lift unless a station is within 40 m
field_notes.ski_area: one feature: the resort's ski-area polygon, or for a resort of several mountains on one map (resorts.json ski_area as a list) one multipolygon, the union of their polygons (a border two of them share is not drawn), named after the resort; or, for a resort with no landuse=winter_sports polygon in OpenStreetMap (resorts.json ski_area "derived"), one multipolygon derived from its own lifts and runs, each buffered by ski_area_buffer_m (100 m by default) and unioned, every hole filled, one polygon per group of lifts and runs whose buffers touch. A listed neighbour's polygon, lifts, runs and stations are never in the file

1.comment: Frozen (MAPS_PLAN D9, ADR-036 M1): what a format-1 pack holds for the app's style. A style may read less, never more; a style that needs anything else needs format 2. test/format.test.mjs pins this object's hash.

2.comment: Frozen (owner decision 2026-10-22, option 2a; docs/MAPS_TRAILVIEW_DESIGN.md section 2): format 1 with the baked hillshade file replaced by an elevation file that the app shades live, so the relief reads right at any bearing. base and ski hold exactly what format 1's hold. dem: 512 px lossless WebP tiles, z9-13, every pixel opaque; encoding mapbox (elevation in metres = -10000 + (R * 65536 + G * 256 + B) * 0.1), each elevation a multiple of step_m. A style may read less, never more. test/format.test.mjs pins this object's hash.

trail_view.comment: The optional pack.json field trail_view (docs/MAPS_TRAILVIEW_DESIGN.md section 3): the bearing a resort's map opens at, so that most runs point from the top of the screen to the bottom, and the terrain's middle and size in that turned frame, for the opening camera. Outside formats: the app's camera reads it, the style does not. write-packs.mjs writes it right after terrain_extent, with exactly these keys in this order, and only on a record whose format has requires_role (a baked hillshade is lit for north up: a pack that carries one never opens turned). Bearing 0 means north up: no trail view. The app reads a trail view that breaks any rule below as none. scripts/lib/trail-view.mjs holds the reader's rule (trailViewOf), the writer's (trailViewProblem), the camera (trailViewCamera), the turned extent (turnedExtent) and the bearing rule (trailBearing); contract-cases.json pins them for the app's port and the pipeline's.

style.comment: How the app's styles carry the shading of every format the app draws, and how staging picks a pack's (scripts/lib/style-contract.mjs, ported by MapAssets.buildStyle; docs/MAPS_TRAILVIEW_DESIGN.md section 4). Metadata source_roles names each source's role; format_layers lists, under each format the style draws, the layers drawn only for that format's packs: a layer listed under no format is drawn for every format, and a style without the key draws format 1 only. shading names each format's shading layer and its source.
